translations.ai.system.answer_exact: Identify what the user is actually asking and answer that first. If they ask for practical advice, give a clear recommendation supported by the data.
translations.ai.system.context_first: Use the weather data provided in the context first. Do not invent missing values.
translations.ai.system.conversation: Use the conversation history to understand references and follow-up questions. Answer the latest request rather than giving a generic forecast.
translations.ai.system.distinguish: Clearly distinguish available data, estimates and advice. Be practical, concise and cautious.
translations.ai.system.emergencies: For emergencies or warnings, advise consulting authorities and official weather services.
translations.ai.system.final_answer_only: Return only the final user-facing answer. Do not output safety classifications, internal reasoning, technical labels, or metadata.
translations.ai.system.general_scope: When the user has chosen AI mode, you may also answer general non-weather questions. Use the app weather context only when it is relevant to the request and do not force it into answers on other topics.
translations.ai.system.identity: You are MeteoNexa AI, a weather and travel assistant. Answer in {language}.
translations.ai.system.intelligence_quality: When Intelligence Quality data is available, clearly distinguish model consensus, historical calibration, run-to-run changes, source freshness and Decision Engine windows. Do not turn agreement or Brier Score into certainty and do not invent missing data.
translations.ai.system.no_fake_live: Do not claim to have consulted live data other than what is in the context.
translations.ai.system.no_markdown: Reply in plain text only. Do not use Markdown, bold asterisks, underscores, backticks, # headings, code fences or Markdown link syntax.
translations.ai.system.no_repeat: Do not repeat the same wording or facts already provided unless necessary. In follow-up answers, add a useful new comparison, trend or detail.
translations.ai.system.style: Prefer 2-5 concise sentences. When useful, cite times and numerical values from the context. Avoid generic introductions, filler and repetitive conclusions.
translations.ai.system.time_reasoning: Interpret relative dates and times using generatedAt and the context timezone. If the requested time is outside the available data coverage, say so.
translations.ai.system.tool_orchestration: Use only the supplied weather evidence. The deterministic MeteoNexa engine decision is authoritative: explain it clearly, do not replace it, and do not invent data, sources, ETAs or risks. If evidence is insufficient, say so.

translations.cookie.access_location.copy: The approximate location shown in “Devices and access” does not use an additional cookie. If you grant browser geolocation permission, MeteoNexa sends only coordinates rounded to one decimal to its own backend and retains them in access history for at most 30 days.
translations.cookie.account_sync.copy: Cross-device synchronization uses the authentication session already described and server-side data; it does not add cookies.
translations.cookie.analytics.copy: MeteoNexa uses Plausible for aggregate, sanitized pageviews. Plausible sets no analytics cookies in the browser and MeteoNexa does not use it for advertising, profiling, or cross-site tracking.
translations.cookie.analytics.preference: The only analytics preference stored by MeteoNexa is the optional local opt-out (meteonexa_analytics_optout_v1). It does not identify the user and is used only to stop pageviews from that browser.
translations.cookie.analytics.title: Cookieless analytics
translations.cookie.client.copy: meteonexa_client is an HttpOnly technical identifier used to synchronise language, theme and preferences. meteonexa_language is a first-party technical cookie used by both the installer and the main PWA to keep language consistent across runtime/standalone pages; it is not used for profiling.
translations.cookie.client.title: Technical preferences
translations.cookie.feedback.copy: “Report a bug” adds no cookies. Text and optional images/videos are sent to the server and delivered by email without being stored in application storage; rate limiting uses only an HMAC reference of the IP. Contact email and diagnostics are optional; video recording uses browser permissions only after an explicit action.
translations.cookie.feedback.media: Attaching or recording images/videos creates no cookies. Camera and microphone permissions are browser/device permissions, not cookies, and are requested only for a recording started by the user.
translations.cookie.forecast_fusion: The Overview reliability fusion creates no dedicated cookie: the request to its same-origin endpoint is made without session/client cookies and without credentials or device identifiers. The weather consensus is therefore the same for guests and authenticated users and is not personalised through an account.
translations.cookie.guest.official_alerts.copy: Viewing warnings as a guest adds no cookie. MeteoNexa uses the selected location for its own endpoint and may serve a recent server-side cache during brief provider outages; no account session or push profile is created.
translations.cookie.intel.features: Intelligence, Decision Timeline, probabilistic nowcast, Local Accuracy, Watch My Plan and Copilot do not add analytics cookies or persistent tracking identifiers. Weather evidence is processed through the documented MeteoNexa server-side endpoints.
translations.cookie.intro: MeteoNexa uses only technical cookies required for operation, security and preferences. It does not use advertising or profiling cookies.
translations.cookie.login.dynamic_weather: The dynamic sign-in background uses only weather data already present in the localStorage described in this policy and adds no cookie, geolocation request or extra weather call before access.
translations.cookie.manage.copy: You can clear data and cookies in your browser settings. MeteoNexa’s “Clear cache/data” command also revokes the session and trusted device when applicable.
translations.cookie.manage.title: How to manage them
translations.cookie.metrics.copy: Product Metrics use no analytics cookies or analytics local/session storage. The client keeps counters temporarily in memory only and sends them to the same origin with credentials=omit; the server stores only date, event name, and aggregated count.
translations.cookie.pipeline.copy: The server-side weather pipeline adds no cookies. It uses server-side locations and preferences already associated with features enabled by the user and may continue through cron/workers while the PWA is closed.
translations.cookie.private_browsing.copy: In private browsing, cookies and storage are separate from the normal session and are usually deleted when the private window closes. MeteoNexa therefore treats incognito as a new device and requires OTP; after sign-in it uses the same technical cookies and Account Sync without adding cookie categories.
translations.cookie.release.current: MeteoNexa 20.1 adds Plausible Analytics without analytics cookies, advertising or profiling. Any opt-out is remembered only as a local browser preference.

translations.privacy.access_history.copy: For email accounts MeteoNexa retains successful access history for at most 30 days to show connected devices and allow remote revocation. Device/browser type, times, timezone, encrypted IP and an approximate location are recorded when supplied by hosting or, after browser permission, derived from coordinates rounded to one decimal. No external IP-geolocation service is queried. You can delete ended-access history early; active sessions are not removed by that operation.
translations.privacy.access_history.revoke_scope: Disconnecting a device revokes only that browser’s session and trusted-device credential: it is not the same as clearing cache, theme, language or other site data. On the remote device, authentication HttpOnly cookies become unusable immediately and are cleared on the next server contact.

translations.privacy.ai.activation: AI calls happen only after an explicit choice: “Switch to AI”, “Generate now” in the briefing, enabling automatic briefing, or enabling Proactive AI.
translations.privacy.ai.advice: Do not enter unnecessary personal data or confidential information in the assistant. You can return to the local engine at any time.
translations.privacy.ai.auth.disabled: External AI features are disabled by this installation’s configuration. No context is sent to an LLM provider while those services remain disabled.
translations.privacy.ai.briefing_history: To reduce repetition, the Briefing may also send the previous briefing text to the provider and, only for selected activities, the impact score, best window and a short reason. No account identifiers or precise coordinates are added.
translations.privacy.ai.data_excluded: Email addresses, session tokens, deviceId/deviceKey values, API keys and arbitrary browser-provided fields are not sent to the provider.
translations.privacy.ai.data_sent: Sent context may include location name, time zone, current conditions, forecasts, nowcast, forecast changes, canonical model consensus, official-warning summaries, convective-risk evidence, aggregate local trust metrics, route risk and wind/crosswind summaries, and selected activity names. Precise or sampled route coordinates are excluded.
translations.privacy.ai.external_service: OpenRouter + NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super (free): only after voluntarily switching to AI mode or for Personal AI Briefing when an authenticated user explicitly enables it.
translations.privacy.ai.external_service.disabled: External AI provider: not configured or disabled for this installation. No request is sent to OpenRouter/Groq until the service is configured and enabled.
translations.privacy.ai.external_service.guest: OpenRouter and LLM providers: they are not contacted during guest access. Their endpoints require an authenticated email session and device proof.
translations.privacy.ai.fact.copy: The assistant stays local until you choose “Switch to AI”. Briefing and Proactive AI are separate opt-in paths. AI flows may process messages and sanitised weather context; email, tokens, device keys, API keys and precise coordinates are not forwarded.
translations.privacy.ai.fact.guest.copy: In guest mode MeteoNexa does not contact OpenRouter or LLM providers. Predictive radar, nowcast and other visible analyses use weather data and local or public processing; external AI features require email sign-in.
translations.privacy.ai.fact.guest.title: No external AI for guests
translations.privacy.ai.fact.title: External AI only on request
translations.privacy.ai.guest.external: No message or weather context is sent to OpenRouter or other LLM providers during a guest session.
translations.privacy.ai.guest.intro: External AI features are not available in guest access. Visible processing such as nowcast and predictive radar runs without sending requests to an LLM provider.
translations.privacy.ai.intro: MeteoNexa uses the local engine by default. If it cannot answer, it may offer AI mode. Separately, authenticated users can enable Personal AI Briefing and Proactive AI based on changes, risks and activities.
translations.privacy.ai.orchestration: AI Weather Copilot receives a weather decision already determined by the MeteoNexa backend. The language-model provider may explain structured weather evidence such as consensus, nowcast, official warnings, convective risk, aggregate trust metrics and route wind/crosswind risk, but it does not calculate the authoritative decision. Sampled route coordinates remain inside the MeteoNexa weather engine and are excluded from the LLM payload.
translations.privacy.ai.proactive: Proactive AI is optional. If enabled, MeteoNexa may call the AI provider when it detects forecast changes, risks or useful windows for selected activities. Daily limits apply and no account identifiers or precise coordinates are forwarded.
translations.privacy.ai.provider_processing: AI requests go from the MeteoNexa backend to OpenRouter and, in the standard free configuration, to NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super (free). OpenRouter and NVIDIA may process content and technical metadata under their respective notices; NVIDIA states that its free endpoint logs data for security and service improvement and advises against sending personal or confidential data.
translations.privacy.ai.severe_context8: For email users who enable proactive AI, a severe event already validated by the deterministic weather engine may be included in the context sent to the AI provider: event type, severity, confidence, title/text and time or ETA. AI does not decide the alert trigger, and this context does not include precise coordinates, account identifiers or device credentials.
translations.privacy.ai.short_notice: The assistant uses the local engine first. OpenRouter is contacted only after “Switch to AI” or in AI paths you explicitly enable: Personal AI Briefing and Proactive AI. Only strictly necessary context is sent.
translations.privacy.ai.short_notice.guest: As a guest, no calls are made to OpenRouter or other LLM providers. External AI features become available only after email sign-in and remain controlled by explicit actions or opt-ins.

translations.privacy.analytics.copy: MeteoNexa sends Plausible only pageviews with sanitized paths (for example /home or /radar). Coordinates, selected location, account/device ID, search queries, AI text and route details are not sent. Only allowed campaign parameters may be retained and the referrer is reduced to its origin. The browser contacts plausible.io, so IP address and User-Agent technically transit in the request; Plausible states that it does not store them in raw form and uses a non-persistent daily identifier.
translations.privacy.analytics.fact.copy: Plausible measures aggregate traffic and viewed pages using sanitized URLs, with no analytics cookies, profiling, or persistent identifiers.
translations.privacy.analytics.fact.title: Privacy-friendly analytics
translations.privacy.analytics.optout: You can disable analytics in the Privacy Center. The opt-out preference is stored only in localStorage as a browser setting; MeteoNexa also respects Global Privacy Control and Do Not Track.
translations.privacy.analytics.processing.basis: Controller’s legitimate interest in measuring and improving the service, with minimization and an available opt-out
translations.privacy.analytics.processing.data: Sanitized pageviews, allowed campaign parameters, referrer reduced to its origin, and technical HTTP metadata required for the request
translations.privacy.analytics.processing.purpose: Measure traffic, most-viewed pages and aggregate acquisition without creating individual profiles
translations.privacy.analytics.processing.retention: According to the Plausible account configuration; no persistent MeteoNexa visitor identifier and Plausible’s visitor salt rotates daily
translations.privacy.analytics.short_notice: We also use aggregate traffic statistics with Plausible, without analytics cookies or profiling. You can disable them in the Privacy Center.
translations.privacy.analytics.status.signal: Disabled by the browser privacy signal (GPC/DNT)
translations.privacy.analytics.title: Traffic analytics with Plausible
translations.privacy.analytics.toggle.copy: Allow aggregate statistics with Plausible. MeteoNexa Product Metrics remain separate and first-party.
translations.privacy.analytics.toggle.title: Traffic analytics
translations.privacy.art13.automated.copy: MeteoNexa does not make automated decisions under Article 22 GDPR that produce legal or similarly significant effects on a person. Weather engines, alerts and AI provide information and suggestions and do not make legal decisions about the user.
translations.privacy.art13.automated.title: Automated decision-making and profiling
translations.privacy.art13.complaint.copy: You have the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority. In Italy you may contact the Garante per la protezione dei dati personali under Article 77 GDPR, without prejudice to other administrative or judicial remedies.
translations.privacy.art13.complaint.link: How to lodge a complaint with the Italian Data Protection Authority
translations.privacy.art13.complaint.title: Complaint to a supervisory authority
translations.privacy.art13.consent.copy: For processing based on consent, you may withdraw consent at any time by disabling the relevant feature or contacting the Controller. Withdrawal does not affect the lawfulness of processing carried out before withdrawal.
translations.privacy.art13.consent.title: Withdrawal of consent
translations.privacy.art13.contact_reminder.copy: To exercise your rights or ask about personal-data processing, use the privacy contact address shown on this page. A request may concern only a specific processing activity or a specific device.
translations.privacy.art13.contact_reminder.title: Privacy contact and data requests
translations.privacy.art13.controller.configuration_m: The controller legal identity is not fully configured for this deployment. Configure the legal name, address and privacy contact before publishing this notice.
translations.privacy.art13.controller.copy: The identity and contact details of the controller configured for this deployment are shown below. A production deployment must configure the legal name, address and privacy contact before publishing this notice.
translations.privacy.art13.controller.title: Data controller
translations.privacy.art13.dpo.configured: The DPO contact configured for this deployment is shown below.
translations.privacy.art13.dpo.copy: No dedicated Data Protection Officer (DPO) is indicated for this installation. If one is appointed or the appointment becomes applicable, the relevant contact details will be published in this notice.
translations.privacy.art13.dpo.title: DPO
translations.privacy.art13.further.copy: If the Controller intends to use the data for a further or different purpose, before that new processing it will provide the information required by Article 13(3) GDPR and update this notice.
translations.privacy.art13.further.title: Further processing purposes
translations.privacy.art13.processing.email.basis: Article 6(1)(b) GDPR: performance of the service requested by the user.
translations.privacy.art13.processing.email.data: Email; identity and OTP hashes/HMACs; timestamps and attempts; anti-abuse IP hash.
translations.privacy.art13.processing.email.purpose: Send the OTP, verify sign-in and create or maintain the session requested by the user.
translations.privacy.art13.processing.email.retention: OTP: up to 10 minutes and in any case until verification/use or expiry. Email session: up to 30 days and, by default, invalidated after 7 consecutive days of inactivity; sign-out or revocation ends it earlier. Trusted device: up to 30 days unless revoked or expired earlier.
translations.privacy.art13.processing.feedback.basis: Controller’s legitimate interest in service security, quality and maintenance (GDPR Art. 6(1)(f)); the optional email is processed only for follow-up related to the report.
translations.privacy.art13.processing.feedback.data: Bug reports: category, title, description and steps entered by the user; contact email only when provided; minimal diagnostics only when authorised; images or videos only when voluntarily attached. The IP address is used only in HMAC form for abuse prevention.
translations.privacy.art13.processing.feedback.purpos: Receive, reproduce and fix malfunctions, protect the service from abuse and contact the user only when they voluntarily provide an email address.
translations.privacy.art13.processing.feedback.retent: Report content and attachments are not stored in the application database or storage: files remain temporary during upload and email delivery. The email copy and attachments remain in the support mailbox only as long as needed to handle the bug and applicable administrative or security needs.
translations.privacy.art13.processing.metrics.basis: Controller’s legitimate interest in improving and measuring the service (Article 6(1)(f) GDPR), with minimisation and aggregation; no analytics cookies or persistent identifiers.
translations.privacy.art13.processing.metrics.data: Daily aggregated feature-usage counts (without identifiers, coordinates, queries, or AI text)
translations.privacy.art13.processing.metrics.purpose: Measure feature adoption and usage, identify areas to improve, and guide product quality using aggregated data.
translations.privacy.art13.processing.metrics.retenti: Maximum 180 days for daily aggregated counts; no per-user or per-device analytics history.
translations.privacy.art13.processing.optional.basis: Article 6(1)(a) GDPR for features based on consent/opt-in; where a feature is requested as part of the service, Article 6(1)(b). Activation can be withdrawn at any time.
translations.privacy.art13.processing.optional.data: Web Push subscription; technical notification metadata and delivered/read/dismissed status per device; Netatmo OAuth tokens; messages and sanitised weather context sent to external AI when enabled.
translations.privacy.art13.processing.optional.purpos: Provide optional notifications, integrations and AI features enabled by the user.
translations.privacy.art13.processing.optional.retent: Push subscription and integrations: until disabled, revoked or technically expired. Notification inbox: removed when the event expires; dismissed after 1 day, read after 3 days, unread within 14 days. MeteoNexa does not keep a general AI-chat history on its backend; any data held by external providers follow their terms and the settings applied.
translations.privacy.art13.processing.personal.basis: Article 6(1)(b) GDPR: performance of service features requested by the user.
translations.privacy.art13.processing.personal.data: Favorites, Home/Work locations, alert profile, activity thresholds and personal preferences.
translations.privacy.art13.processing.personal.purpos: Personalize Decision Engine, Route Weather and Smart Alerts and synchronize these settings across authenticated devices.
translations.privacy.art13.processing.personal.retent: Until deleted by the user or the service is discontinued.
translations.privacy.art13.processing.security.basis: Article 6(1)(f) GDPR: the Controller’s legitimate interest in service security, fraud/abuse prevention and access management. Processing is limited to data technically necessary for those purposes.
translations.privacy.art13.processing.security.data: Device ID/proof; session/trusted-device HMAC; device type, system/browser, Web/PWA, timezone, encrypted IP and, when available, approximate location from hosting headers or authorized browser geolocation rounded to one decimal.
translations.privacy.art13.processing.security.purpos: Protect sessions and devices, prevent abuse, show sign-ins and allow remote device revocation.
translations.privacy.art13.processing.security.retent: Active devices: for the lifetime of the session/trust. Ended-access history: at most 30 days, with per-identity quantity limits and the option to delete it earlier.
translations.privacy.art13.processing.title: Processing connected with email sign-in
translations.privacy.art13.provision.copy: Providing your email address is optional, but it is necessary if you want to use email sign-in and restricted features. If you do not provide it, you can continue using features available in guest mode. Technical data strictly necessary for security are processed when you use the authenticated service.
translations.privacy.art13.provision.title: Whether providing data is required
translations.privacy.art13.recipients.copy: Data may be processed by technical providers necessary to the service: hosting/server providers, email/SMTP transport, browser Web Push services, weather/map providers, Netatmo when connected, and OpenRouter/model providers only when AI is enabled. Data are not sold or disclosed for advertising purposes. Providers act as processors or independent controllers according to their respective roles.
translations.privacy.art13.recipients.title: Recipients and categories of recipients
translations.privacy.art13.rights.copy: Under Articles 15-22 GDPR you may request access, rectification, erasure, restriction and, where applicable, portability; you may also object to processing based on legitimate interests. Send requests to the privacy contact address shown on this page. The Controller responds within the time limits in Article 12 GDPR, normally within one month.
translations.privacy.art13.rights.title: Your rights
translations.privacy.art13.scope: This section describes processing connected with email sign-in and MeteoNexa’s restricted features. It is provided under Article 13 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 and should be read together with the technical sections below.
translations.privacy.art13.title: Information under Article 13 GDPR
translations.privacy.art13.transfers.copy: Some technical or AI providers may process data outside the European Economic Area depending on the services enabled by the operator. Where applicable, transfers must rely on the provider’s documented safeguards and an appropriate mechanism under Articles 45-49 GDPR. The links shown below reflect the configured external AI provider.
translations.privacy.art13.transfers.groq_link: Groq privacy policy and transfer information
translations.privacy.art13.transfers.openrouter_link: OpenRouter privacy notice and transfer safeguards
translations.privacy.art13.transfers.title: Transfers outside the EEA
translations.privacy.auth.trusted_reentry: When you choose Email, MeteoNexa may first check whether this browser is already a trusted device. The server verifies the HttpOnly trusted cookie, device ID and browser-held device proof; only when all match is a new session created without sending an OTP. Otherwise the normal email-code flow is shown.
translations.privacy.bigdatacloud_reverse_geocoding_c: BigDataCloud for reverse geocoding, with coordinates-only fallback.
translations.privacy.cache.email.address_use.auth: The receipt was sent to the authenticated session address; the browser cannot select a different recipient.
translations.privacy.cache.email.address_use.guest: The address you entered was used only to send this receipt and did not create an account or email session. For abuse prevention, only a non-reversible HMAC identifier may be used in technical counters.
translations.privacy.cache.email.card.copy.auth: MeteoNexa removed its accessible local data, the device credential and local personal data; it also asked the browser to remove Cache Storage, IndexedDB and the Service Worker. The server session and trusted device were revoked. Only language and theme remain as interface preferences.
translations.privacy.cache.email.card.copy.guest: MeteoNexa removed its accessible local data, including location, favourites, thresholds, stored weather data and device identifiers; it also asked the browser to remove Cache Storage, IndexedDB and the Service Worker. Only language and theme remain as interface preferences.
translations.privacy.cache.email.card.title: Local application data removed
translations.privacy.cache.email.footer: The receipt contains no location, coordinates, favourites, tokens, credentials or other personal app data.
translations.privacy.cache.email.heading: Privacy reset complete
translations.privacy.cache.email.intro.auth: MeteoNexa local-data deletion has completed on this device and the associated email session has been closed.
translations.privacy.cache.email.intro.guest: MeteoNexa local-data deletion has completed on this device in guest mode.
translations.privacy.cache.email.retention: For security and abuse prevention, technical logs and pseudonymised counters may remain on the server under the normal retention periods. This receipt does not certify deletion of logs the operator must retain for security or applicable obligations.
translations.privacy.cache.email.subject: MeteoNexa — privacy reset confirmation
translations.privacy.cache.guest_verification: For a guest privacy reset, the email address is verified with a one-time code before deletion and the receipt. The code does not create an account and the verification token expires quickly.
translations.privacy.cache.verify.email.heading: Confirm your email address
translations.privacy.cache.verify.email.instructions: Use this code within {minutes} minutes to confirm that you control the address. MeteoNexa can send the deletion receipt only after verification.
translations.privacy.cache.verify.email.plain: MeteoNexa code: {code}. It is valid for {minutes} minutes and is used only to verify the privacy receipt.
translations.privacy.cache.verify.email.safety: If you did not request this verification, ignore this message: no account is created and no deletion is confirmed in your name.
translations.privacy.cache.verify.email.subject: MeteoNexa · Confirm email for data deletion
translations.privacy.can_sign_out_remove_session_dele: You can sign out to remove the session, or delete cookies, local storage, and site data in your browser settings. Deleting the technical cookie disconnects the browser from the language and theme preferences stored on the server; a new identifier will be created on the next visit.
translations.privacy.context.auth.copy: This email session can use enabled private features. Each service remains subject to its settings, explicit actions or opt-ins, and backend authorization.
translations.privacy.context.auth.title: Privacy notice for authenticated users
translations.privacy.context.guest.copy: You are using MeteoNexa as a guest. External AI assistant, AI Briefing, proactive AI, personal history, devices, push notifications, integrations and accuracy learning are not used in this session. Only public and technical services required by visible features remain active.
translations.privacy.context.guest.title: Privacy notice for guest access
translations.privacy.context.loading.copy: MeteoNexa is adapting this notice to the features available in this session.
translations.privacy.context.loading.title: Checking access context
translations.privacy.context.offline.copy: The browser remembers a previous email sign-in, but while offline MeteoNexa cannot verify the server session. Private remote services, external AI, Web Push and integrations are not contacted until connectivity and the session are verified again.
translations.privacy.context.offline.title: Remembered email session · offline
translations.privacy.cookie.client.characteristics: First-party technical cookie, HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict. It is not used to track browsing or build profiles.
translations.privacy.during_these_connections_provide: During these connections, providers may receive standard technical request data such as the IP address, user agent, date, and time. MeteoNexa does not add advertising identifiers.
translations.privacy.email.auth: You signed in by email. The backend uses the address for OTP and maintains a server-side session bound to device proof; the cookie token is HttpOnly and only its HMAC/hash is stored in the database. Expired OTP records are removed automatically.
translations.privacy.email.auth.v2: You signed in by email. The backend uses the address for OTP through the available email transport and maintains a server-side session bound to device proof; the cookie is HttpOnly and only the token HMAC/hash is stored in the database. Expired OTP records are deleted automatically.
translations.privacy.email.disabled: Email transport is not available in this installation. Until SMTP is configured in the database or a valid local mail transport is available, MeteoNexa cannot send OTP codes and sends no email.
translations.privacy.email.guest: No email sign-in is active in this guest session. Only if you voluntarily request a sign-in code does the backend use the email address to send an OTP through the configured SMTP transport; it temporarily stores the code hash, timestamps, attempts and IP hash under the security limits.
translations.privacy.email.guest.v2: No email sign-in is in use in this guest session. Only if you voluntarily request a sign-in code does the backend use the address to send an OTP through the available email transport; code hash, timestamps, attempts and IP hash are kept temporarily under the security limits.
translations.privacy.email.loading: Session status is checked before showing details about email sign-in.
translations.privacy.ensemble.guest: Guest access does not feed the persistent forecast/observation sampling used for adaptive accuracy for authenticated users.
translations.privacy.ensemble.learning: For authenticated users, Verified Trust calibration uses server-side samples of forecasts and reference weather data, associated with device and area/location, to estimate skill, error and Brier score by phenomenon and lead time. Samples contain only the required weather metrics; retention is server-configurable, with a 180-day default within the configured limits.
translations.privacy.external.analytics: Plausible Analytics for aggregate traffic statistics: no analytics cookies or persistent identifiers; Plausible states that visitor data is processed and stored in the EU.
translations.privacy.external.cartography: Mapping: when you display a map, the browser may request map style and tiles directly from OpenFreeMap, which receives normal HTTP request metadata (for example IP address and user-agent). OpenStreetMap and Natural Earth are map-data/attribution sources and are not presented as endpoints that the browser necessarily contacts directly.
translations.privacy.external.github_boundaries: Italian administrative-boundary datasets are requested by the browser only from MeteoNexa. The backend retrieves them from an allowlisted source, validates them and stores them in protected cache; the browser does not contact raw.githubusercontent.com directly.
translations.privacy.external.lightning: XWeather, when configured, for lightning data used by advanced features and as a supporting signal for the Severe Weather Monitor.
translations.privacy.external.nasa_gibs: NASA GIBS: contacted directly by the browser only when you enable the satellite layer. Tile requests may disclose normal HTTP technical metadata to NASA GIBS (for example IP address, user-agent, date/time and requested tile). The layer is not preloaded when you do not use it.
translations.privacy.external.netatmo: Netatmo only when an authenticated user voluntarily connects their account/station; OAuth and tokens are handled by the backend and tokens are encrypted in the database.
translations.privacy.external.push: Browser Web Push services (Mozilla, Google/FCM or Apple depending on the device) only after an authenticated user explicitly enables push notifications.
translations.privacy.external.radar_backend: LibreWXR for radar metadata and images: requests to the radar provider are made by the MeteoNexa backend, and authorized tiles are served to the app through signed, cached internal endpoints.
translations.privacy.external.reverse_geocoding8: Reverse geocoding (BigDataCloud): after you grant geolocation permission, the browser sends coordinates to a same-origin MeteoNexa endpoint without account or device credentials. The backend rounds them to 3 decimals before querying BigDataCloud. The provider receives approximate coordinates and the server’s technical HTTP metadata, not the browser IP address. The response is used only to associate a place name with the position.
translations.privacy.external.ui_libraries: cdnjs.cloudflare.com for the MapLibre GL and Choices.js libraries loaded by the interface.
translations.privacy.feedback.copy: For “Report a bug”, the browser sends only completed fields and any images/videos selected by the user. “Record screen” uses the Screen Capture API only after an explicit user action: the surface is chosen in the browser/OS picker; MeteoNexa does not open the camera and does not record in the background. If screen capture is unavailable, the user can use the system recorder and attach the file. The recipient is a support mailbox configured only on the server; if it is not set, the privacy contact is used and, as a final fallback, the SMTP sender mailbox. The browser cannot choose the recipient. The IP address is not included in the email and is used only in HMAC form for anti-abuse rate limiting.
translations.privacy.feedback.media: Images and videos are optional. If you choose “Record video”, the browser requests camera and microphone access only after your action; MeteoNexa does not start background recordings. Files are checked by the server, used to build the support email and are not copied to application storage or the application database.
translations.privacy.forecast_fusion: Overview reliability: for guests and authenticated users, the selected location coordinates, reduced to 3 decimal places, are sent to a same-origin MeteoNexa endpoint through a request without session/client cookies or device proof to compute deterministic consensus across six Open-Meteo models. The endpoint uses no account data or external AI and does not save the location/result as a user profile. Provider responses are held in the same server-side technical cache used by Intelligence for resilience; stale snapshots may be used as fallback for at most 6 hours and a stale/degraded fusion cannot override the base Overview forecast.
translations.privacy.guest.official_alerts: In guest mode MeteoNexa allows public warnings to be viewed for the selected location. The request sends only the location/coordinates needed for matching to the MeteoNexa backend; no email, Account Sync, external AI or notification profile is required. For continuity, the backend may temporarily reuse a MeteoAlarm cache or a recent server-side snapshot already produced by the pipeline for the same area, without creating account data. Push and personal thresholds remain email-only.
translations.privacy.intel.aifs: The consensus may include ECMWF AIFS, an AI weather model queried through Open-Meteo. AIFS is a numerical/AI forecast source and does not use the assistant language model; radar and local observations remain the priority for nowcasting.
translations.privacy.intel.copilot: Meteo Copilot uses server-side MeteoNexa tools to compute weather, nowcast, confidence and Weather Twin results. When an external LLM provider is used, it receives structured and sanitised weather results, timestamps and sources; precise coordinates, account/device identifiers and credentials are excluded from the LLM payload.
translations.privacy.intel.route: Route Weather 3.0 samples up to 24 points along a route. The sampled points are sent by the MeteoNexa server to the Open-Meteo weather provider to obtain conditions along the journey; the browser no longer makes these route-weather requests directly. The data is used only for the requested feature and does not introduce advertising tracking.
translations.privacy.intel.twin: Personal Weather Twin uses activity thresholds stored in the account (for example running, cycling, motorcycle, sea, worksite, commuting, kids or pets) to calculate personal weather windows. These preferences remain account configuration data and are not used for advertising or commercial profiling.
translations.privacy.intelq.saved_locations: If you choose to save multiple locations while authenticated, MeteoNexa stores up to 8 locations server-side for the device: role (for example Home/Work/Family), label, location/administrative name, coordinates rounded to 5 decimal places and timezone. You can delete them from the app; they are not created for guests.
translations.privacy.intro.current: MeteoNexa processes only the data required to provide forecasts, alerts, account synchronization and features requested by the user. Deterministic weather processing remains separate from any AI explanation.
translations.privacy.language_theme.storage: Browser language and theme are sent to the internal API and stored in the application database with the browser’s technical identifier. On startup the app synchronizes preferences and updated translations; these responses are not stored in the Cache API.
translations.privacy.latest_weather_air_quality_data_: Latest weather and air-quality data, also used offline.
translations.privacy.links_browser_language_theme_pre: Links the browser to the language and theme preferences stored in the app database.
translations.privacy.login.dynamic_weather: On the sign-in screen, the weather background uses only the latest weather snapshot already stored locally in this browser and no older than 6 hours. Sign-in does not request geolocation or make extra weather calls before access; the first frame stays neutral until the local scene is resolved, avoiding a flash of the wrong weather condition. If the snapshot is missing or stale, a neutral/night scene based only on device time is used.
translations.privacy.makes_app_available_even_when_co: Makes the app available even when the connection is unavailable or unstable.
translations.privacy.metrics.copy: To measure use of the main features, MeteoNexa records only daily aggregated counts from a closed event allowlist. The analytics dataset does not contain session, email, account, device ID, coordinates, full location name, search query, or AI text. Ordinary network and security logs remain separate from these metrics.
translations.privacy.metrics.title: First-party Product Metrics
translations.privacy.no_advertising_profiling_cookie_: No advertising, profiling, or cookie-consent categories are loaded. The first-access notice remains informational; Product Metrics use no analytics cookies or persistent identifiers.
translations.privacy.notifications.auth: Local notifications require explicit browser permission. If you also enable Web Push, the backend registers the subscription bound to the device and briefly keeps the technical content and read/dismissed state of its inbox; you can disable and remove the subscription at any time.
translations.privacy.notifications.disabled: Private/Web Push notifications are not enabled for this installation or for your access profile. No Push subscription is registered by that service.
translations.privacy.notifications.guest: As a guest you can use only local alerts based on data already available in the app. A guest session does not register a Web Push subscription with the backend or configure private device-bound push checks.
translations.privacy.notifications.guest.v2: In guest mode MeteoNexa does not register Web Push subscriptions on the backend and does not start private weather checks linked to the device. Private notification features require an authenticated email session and explicit opt-in.
translations.privacy.notifications.lifecycle: For the authenticated Web Push inbox, MeteoNexa keeps the technical notification content and its delivered, read or dismissed status per device for a short period: the row is removed when the event expires; dismissed notifications after 1 day, read notifications after 3 days and unread notifications within a maximum of 14 days.
translations.privacy.notifications.loading: Access status is checked before describing the available notifications.
translations.privacy.offline.guest: Offline, a guest keeps the latest available data and safe settings on the device. Login/OTP, external AI, push, integrations and other private operations are not queued.
translations.privacy.offline.sync: While offline, MeteoNexa keeps the latest available data on the device and queues only safe preferences/settings. When the connection returns it attempts to sync them with the database and refresh APIs. Login/OTP, AI requests, push, OAuth/Netatmo and other sensitive operations are never queued offline.
translations.privacy.open_meteo_forecasts_location_se: Open-Meteo for forecasts, location search, and air quality.
translations.privacy.personal.account_sync: Account Sync: Home/Work, saved locations, favorites, alert profile and activity thresholds can be synchronized across devices authenticated with the same email. The sync identity is a server-side HMAC of the email; plaintext email is not stored in sync tables.
translations.privacy.pipeline.retention: The pipeline retains technical worker/provider telemetry for up to 30 days, Lightning aggregates linked to location/device for up to 14 days and official-warning revisions for up to 180 days; inactive current-warning state is pruned after 30 days. Technical run details use hashed references and do not store email addresses or API keys. Calibration evidence follows the Forecast Reliability retention already described.
translations.privacy.pipeline.server_side: For authenticated users who enable locations, Radar or Smart Alerts, MeteoNexa may run a periodic server-side weather pipeline even while the PWA is closed: it checks official warnings, independent observations, configured Lightning, the Radar archive and forecast verification/calibration. The LLM is not run automatically by this pipeline.
translations.privacy.precise_location_requested_only_: Precise location is requested only after an explicit action. The browser displays its own permission request. The selected coordinates are used to obtain forecasts, air quality, radar, and the location name.
translations.privacy.private_browsing: Private/incognito windows are treated as a new device because cookies, device proof and storage are isolated from the normal browser profile. For security they are not automatically recognized as trusted devices: a new OTP is required. After the same email is verified, MeteoNexa restores Account Sync, favorites, saved locations, alerts and thresholds; when a Home/Work location exists the app can resume directly. Local private-browsing data is removed when the private session closes according to browser behavior.
translations.privacy.provide_weather_mapping_features: To provide weather and mapping features, the browser connects directly to the following services:
translations.privacy.radar.predictive: Predictive radar analyses movement between radar frames already loaded in the browser to estimate direction, speed and possible rain arrival. The result is a short-term estimate with a confidence level, not a new radar observation.
translations.privacy.release.current: MeteoNexa 20.1 adds Analytics & Observability with Plausible using cookieless, sanitized pageviews. First-party Product Metrics, the weather engine and decisions remain separate; no coordinates, queries, AI text or account/device identifiers are sent to Plausible.
translations.privacy.section.reliability.title: Verified precision and reliability metrics
translations.privacy.severe.monitor5: Severe Weather Monitor: Overview may check at short intervals for forecast signals of hail, thunderstorms, snow, strong wind, ice, severe fog and extreme heat. The public read-only request uses no account, session or device identifier, reduces coordinates to 3 decimals and does not store them as account data. It uses Open-Meteo and, when configured, XWeather lightning through the backend and technical cache. Stale/degraded provider data cannot create new severe warnings. Official warnings remain a separate, higher-priority channel.
translations.privacy.sign_session_email_sign_email_ad: Sign-in session and, for email sign-in, email address, display name, and session token.
translations.privacy.smart.alerts: Smart Alerts are opt-in and only for authenticated users. The server periodically evaluates weather events and keeps a limited technical event/deduplication log; alert decisions are deterministic and are not delegated to the LLM.
translations.privacy.smart.demo: the guest demo does not use external AI or account data; coordinates are rounded to roughly 1 km before server-side weather requests and are not stored in the database.
translations.privacy.smart.official: Official warnings are shown separately from MeteoNexa forecasts. When authorized MeteoAlarm EDR access is configured, MeteoNexa uses GeoJSON geometry and a point-in-area check for the location; otherwise it uses the public Atom feed with conservative textual matching. Neither mode replaces communications from competent authorities.
translations.privacy.storage.local_settings: Local interface preferences remain on the device: language, theme, UI settings and local read markers for current alerts are stored in browser localStorage. For authenticated users, language and theme may also be synchronized with the internal API as described below.
translations.privacy.storage.session.guest: Local guest-session indicator and interface state. No email address is stored and no email-session token is created.
